_comment: The seal codec and cohort verifier. Its own spec because a spec mutates ONE file, and these guards live in seal.rs rather than the ABI surface in lib.rs. The verifier is the one place in this lane where a surviving mutant means a security check that does not check. MOVED 2026-09-16 with `seal.rs` itself, from `kandelo-image-module` into `runtime-core`, so `rootfs::load_image` can authenticate cohorts at the door every caller passes through — the kernel's boot as well as a builder's derived load. The trials are unchanged; only the file they mutate and the crate they verify against moved. RETIRED 2026-09-16, the empty-payload pair: a second emptiness check was added to `verify_cohorts` when the verifier moved, and `decode` had already returned `SealState::None` for empty bytes since it was written. The trial for it survived because the guard could not fail -- the sixth cause, something else had already decided -- and the guard is deleted rather than given a test. The rule now lives as a comment on the early return that enforces it. AND THE VERIFY NAMES BOTH CRATES, which the move nearly cost. `seal.rs` moved to `runtime-core` and its unit tests went with it, but four trials are about the PRODUCER -- the export door that re-seals -- and the tests that kill those live in `kandelo-image-module`. Repointing the verify at the new crate alone made four trials survive that had been killed for weeks, which reads exactly like a regression and was a spec no longer running the tests that answer it.
verify: scripts/dev-shell.sh cargo test -q -p runtime-core -p kandelo-image-module --target "$(rustc -vV | sed -n 's/^host: //p')" >/dev/null 2>&1

trials.name: a cohort short of its expected count still authenticates
the cohort identity is never checked against its seal
members may disagree about their own cohort
one member name may stand for two archives
the cohort identity depends on declaration order
the cohort identity runs its fields together
a payload with trailing bytes decodes anyway
a payload version this reader does not know is guessed at
the cohort digest is not domain-separated
a pending seal is treated as no seal at all
a pending declaration decodes as an absent seal
a cohort already sealed is left as it is instead of recomputed
the producer seals a cohort short of its declared count
the producer lets members disagree about the cohort size
the producer lets two archives share one member name
a pending declaration's count is dropped in the encoding
